q: How do I open my short film with a slow fade up from black, the sound arriving first?
a: 1. Apply Dip to Black at the very start of the first clip (`sequence.applyVideoTransition` with Dissolve ▸ Dip to Black), lengthened with `sequence.setTransition`: at the start of the sequence its first half stays black and the second half fades up, so a 4 s Dip gives 2 s of black and a 2 s fade (for a fade over the whole length, keyframe Opacity from 0 to 100 % instead). 2. Start the ambience or music a second or two before the picture appears: a J cut, or the audio clip placed earlier with an Exponential Fade from silence. 3. The title over black or over the first shot once it is up.

q: fade in at the start is too short and I can't make it longer
a: A transition needs media beyond the edit; at the start of the sequence lengthen it with `sequence.setTransition`, and if the clip has no spare frames before its In point, keyframe Opacity from 0 to 100 % instead (`effects.toggleAnimation`).

q: Open on black with just a voice, then fade the picture up.
a: Leave a few seconds of black (an empty start or a Black Video clip, `file.newBlackVideo`) with the voice playing, then Dip to Black / Opacity keyframes bring the first shot up under it.

q: How do I add a video-game style HUD over my gameplay-like footage: health bar, score and a mini map?
a: 1. A graphic clip on the top track with shapes and text (`graphics.newRectangle`, `graphics.newText`): a bar background, a coloured health bar, the score in a corner, all inside the safe margins. 2. Animate the health bar with Crop Right keyframes (`effects.toggleAnimation`) as it drops. 3. Change the score with Hold keyframes or by cutting the text clip at each change. 4. A mini map: a small picture-in-picture in a corner with Rounded Crop.

q: hud health bar should flash red when it gets low
a: Duplicate the bar's clip coloured red above it and keyframe its Opacity on and off with Hold interpolation (`effects.setInterpolation`) while the bar is low.

q: Reuse the HUD across a whole series of videos.
a: Save the HUD graphic as a template with the score text editable (graphics templates), pinned elements so they keep their places, and the bar animation as an effect preset.

q: How do I make a watchable video of my kid's school play filmed from the back of a dark hall?
a: 1. Brighten the stage with noise reduction first (`grade.insertNode`, NR luma / chroma), then exposure on the next node; don't push the shadows. 2. Punch in on the performers with Motion Scale / Position where the resolution allows. 3. Audio: Clean Up Voice (`audio.cleanupVoice`) or Voice Isolation on the stage sound; Auto-Match levels across songs and speech. 4. Cut out the long gaps between scenes; titles for the scene names.

q: stage lights make the faces blown out and orange
a: Bring the highlights down with a soft shoulder or soft clip, then cool the stage light's colour on a node with a window or qualifier on the faces; clipped parts stay white.

q: Two parents filmed the play from different seats, combine them.
a: Sync the two cameras by their waveforms (`clip.synchronize`), make a multicam and cut between the angles; match their colour with Shot Match.

q: How do I add an audio description track for blind viewers?
a: 1. Find the gaps in the dialogue where the picture matters (markers on them, `markers.add`). 2. Write a short description per gap and make it a narration clip with Text to Speech (`tts.create`) or record it (`audio.voiceover.start`) on its own track. 3. Duck the music and effects under each description (`essentialSound.generateDucking`), never over dialogue. 4. Export a described version alongside the main one.

q: description doesn't fit in the gap before the next line
a: Shorten the text (`tts.edit` keeps the clip's place) or speed up the voice in the Text to Speech panel; describe only what the viewer needs at that moment.

q: Keep the description voice clearly separate from the film's voices.
a: A different voice from the cast's, kept centred and dry, typed Dialogue on its own track so its level and Clean Up settings stay separate.

q: How do I add a sign language interpreter in a box on my video?
a: 1. Interpreter clip on V2, synced to the speech (`clip.synchronize` or by eye). 2. Motion Scale about 25–35 % and Position in a lower corner, picture-in-picture, inside the safe margins. 3. Large enough to read the hands and face; nothing (captions, lower thirds) over it. 4. Rounded Crop or a plain border to separate it.

q: interpreter was filmed on a messy background
a: Crop it tighter (Crop effect) or, if it was shot on a plain screen, key it with Ultra Key and put a solid Color Matte behind it.

q: Where should captions go when there's also an interpreter box?
a: Keep the box clear: anchor the captions at the top, or align them to the other side, with the caption track's style (`captions.setStyle`: anchor, align, margin), and keep both inside the safe margins.

q: How do I make captions for deaf viewers that include sounds like [door slams] and who is speaking?
a: 1. Create captions from the transcript (`transcript.createCaptions`), with speaker detection on when transcribing. 2. Edit each caption (`captions.setText`) to add speaker names where it isn't obvious and sound cues in brackets, such as [door slams] or [music]. 3. Keep each on screen long enough to read. 4. Export as SRT / WebVTT next to the video (`captions.export`) so viewers can switch them on.

q: captions flash by too fast to read
a: Lengthen them: merge short ones (`captions.merge`) or trim their ends later (`captions.trim`); the default minimum is a second, and text should stay long enough to read twice.

q: Burned-in captions or a separate file for accessibility?
a: A separate SRT / WebVTT file: viewers can turn it on, resize it and translate it; burn in only for autoplaying social clips.

q: How do I film and edit a scene of someone reading an old letter aloud?
a: 1. Cut between close-ups of the handwriting and the reader's face. 2. The reading as a voice-over (`audio.voiceover.start`), close and dry, centred. 3. A slow push-in on the letter with Motion Scale keyframes (`effects.toggleAnimation`). 4. A warm, faded look on the letter shots; quiet room tone or music under the voice.

q: show the words of the letter on screen as she reads them
a: Captions from the transcript of the voice-over (`transcript.createCaptions`), styled like handwriting with a script font (`captions.setStyle`), or text layers timed to each line.

q: Letter voice-over should start before we see the letter.
a: Start the voice-over under the previous shot (a J cut) and cut to the letter a line later; a marker on the cut point helps time it.
